title: SYSK Selects: How Kleptomania Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the 2009 episode on kleptomania. The hosts open with holiday-season theft statistics, including the Global Retail Theft Barometer figures on worldwide and North American retail losses. They explain the APA (DSM) diagnostic criteria that separate kleptomania from ordinary shoplifting, and Josh and Chuck act out a kleptomaniac shopping scenario. They discuss hoarding examples, the Israeli shoplifter case, gender and age patterns, and celebrity shoplifting cases. Treatment options (SSRIs, cognitive and aversion therapy, systematic desensitization, and a nalmefene trial) are covered, along with the brain research on frontal lobe and reward circuitry. The episode closes with a history of the condition from St. Augustine through Matthew's 1816 description, plus a listener mail segment about a man named Hippie Rob.

segments.title: Opening banter and holiday stealing season
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the episode, introducing the 2009 kleptomania topic as a Selects pick. They discuss holiday shoplifting season and the Global Retail Theft Barometer report on rising worldwide and North American retail losses.

segments.title: Shoplifting versus kleptomania and the DSM criteria
segments.summary: The hosts distinguish kleptomania from shoplifting and go through the American Psychiatric Association's DSM criteria: repeated failure to resist the impulse to steal, tension before the theft, relief after, and no anger, revenge, delusion or impaired judgment. Josh and Chuck act out a kleptomaniac scenario.

segments.title: Hoarding and the Israeli shoplifter case
segments.summary: The hosts discuss stolen items that are hoarded or unused, citing an early twentieth century woman and an April case in Israel where a man was found with large quantities of unopened stolen goods. They note his wife and son were suspected of knowing but not acting, and that his planned stickers may argue against kleptomania.

segments.title: Gender, age, and celebrity shoplifting cases
segments.summary: The hosts discuss who is diagnosed with kleptomania, noting women are more often diagnosed, possibly due to underreporting by men. They cover age of onset, elderly shoplifting in Japan, and the celebrity shoplifting case involving Horowitz at Saks Fifth Avenue. They also note that the Justice Department does not accept kleptomania as a defense.

segments.title: Classification, research, and treatments
segments.summary: The hosts discuss whether kleptomania is its own disorder or a symptom of other conditions, and mention related impulse disorders. They cover difficulty finding subjects for research, a Stanford study from 2002, and treatments including SSRIs, cognitive therapy, covert sensitization, aversion therapy, and systematic desensitization. They also describe a 2009 nalmefene trial.

segments.title: Brain research and history of kleptomania
segments.summary: Psychiatrist John Grant's University of Minnesota research is described, including proposed links to serotonin transport, frontal lobe white matter, and the limbic reward system. The hosts then trace the history from St. Augustine through Matthew's 1816 description and Freud's theories.

segments.title: Listener mail: Hippie Rob
segments.summary: A listener writes about a man named Hippie Rob, and the hosts conclude he is not the same Hippie Rob they know, because the real one loves alcohol. They ask listeners for information and invite emails.
